economic/insurer/Peel.caption: The ledger in currency units: declared legs, side totals and results, in ledger order. Signed as booked, so every column adds down the sheet. economic_ratios/insurer/Peel.caption: One row per block, read across: premium written, loss, expense, the margin left, the standard deviation of that margin, and the three ratios the amounts imply. P, L, E and M are signed in the gross direction, so they add across blocks and the identity M = P - L - E holds exactly; loss absorbs cession recoveries and any unclassified obligation leg, and expense absorbs ceding commission, a contra expense. SD is a marginal row property and does not add. LR, ER and CR are ratios of means, the convention of a rate filing, re-derived from each block's own amounts and never averaged from the blocks below, so CR satisfies 1 - CR = M / P on every row. The three bold rows are the positions: gross, the book net of each tier, and the closing net. A net of tier row is the running position through that tier and sits outside the sum, so the footing runs over the steps between them alone. The raw view itemizes the declared legs and adds the expected-ratio columns, which are the same three read as means of ratios and part company with these exactly when premium is random and correlated with loss, the signature of a retro, a swing, a slide or a profit commission.

economic_tail/insurer/Peel.caption: Return period ladder over the closing margin. A payoff, so the adverse tail is the LOW one: the 1 in 200 year is the rung that goes 200-to-1 against you, and the ladder walks into the losses as you read up. VaR is the quoted result at that rung, excess VaR its shortfall against expectation (negative on the downside, which is the capital the state calls for), and VaR to mean the leverage, blank near break-even where the ratio has no content. The 1 in 200 (99.5%, Solvency II) and 1 in 250 (99.6%, US capital adequacy) anchors are emphasized on both sides of the ladder. TVaR is on the raw view only: the library computes the measure above a rung, which on a payoff is the wrong side, so it would read as a tail average and sit near the mean.

economic_waterfall/insurer/Peel.caption: The margin walk: gross, what each layer cedes, and the closing net. Premium spent and Margin spent are the step against the gross block, Margin ratio is the margin per unit of premium, Margin is the expected result, and MSD is that margin over its own standard deviation, a multiple. The bold rows are the positions: gross, the book net of each tier, and the closing net. A net of tier row is the running position through that tier, the book once that tier's program has worked; it restates the rows above it, so the footing runs over the steps between the positions alone. The capital each step calls for, and what that capital costs, are in the table below.

Three capital bases for the same walk, each beside its own cost of capital, all struck at the 1-in-100 state. Capital is the negated result in that state, so a risk-bearing row reads the capital it holds and a ceded row reads a negative number: the capital the cover releases, which is what a cover does. The CoC columns are margin over the capital beside them, on every row, so they read as a return where capital is held and as the price paid per unit released where it is given back, with no change of arithmetic. The reinsurance test is whether a ceded row's CoC comes in under the return the risk-bearing rows earn. Standalone is each step's own 1-in-100, two-sided by role: a risk-bearing step reads its own adverse tail, a ceded step the writer's, the state in which the cover pays most. Tail measures do not add, so standalone does not foot, and its gap against the other two is the diversification benefit. Net conditions on the whole book landing at its own 1-in-100, which decomposes the capital the firm actually holds and is the basis for attribution; gross conditions on the gross result landing at its own, which reads the program as a stress test. Both are ladders of conditional means and foot down the walk where complete. These capital amounts are NOTIONAL: nothing in the ledger is truncated at them, no default is modeled and no loss is limited by them. They are the capital the state calls for, read off a quantile.

validation/insurer/Aggregate.caption: Moment-based validation: computes the theoretical mean (EX), CV or SD and skewness (Sk) of the gross severity and gross compound distribution from the relationships between frequency, severity and compound moments. The theoretical calculation uses analytic expressions for the frequency and for lognormal, gamma, exponential and Pareto severities, and high-accuracy numerical integration for other severities. The FFT approximation's moments (Est) are compared to the theoretical ones, and Err is the noise-aware relative error between them. The theoretical calculation is independent of the FFT, so close agreement is strong evidence the approximation is valid. Rows failing the object's validation_eps gate are emphasized. With reinsurance, Est and Err become Net (or Ceded) and Change, the effect of the cession, so the table no longer validates: validate the gross object.

validation/insurer/BivariateAggregate.caption: Moment QA for the joint grid: the reference moment against the realized marginal and total estimates, with noise aware relative errors. A component failing its marginal mean gate, or a tail deficit over the gate, emphasizes the matching Agg row.

validation/insurer/Distortion.caption: Structural identity checks with gates and verdicts; failing checks are emphasized.

validation/insurer/Peel.caption: Moment QA for the wrapped book: the reference moment against the realized FFT estimate, with noise aware relative errors, for the frequency, severity and aggregate. Errors of this size are discretization, not model error. Empty on a hand-built kernel P&L, which carries no engine.

validation/insurer/Portfolio.caption: Moment-based validation per unit plus the portfolio total: computes the theoretical mean (EX), CV and skewness (Sk) of each unit's severity and compound distribution from the relationships between frequency, severity and compound moments, and the total's by combining the units as independent, which is how the FFT convolves them. The theoretical calculation uses analytic expressions for the frequency and for lognormal, gamma, exponential and Pareto severities, and high-accuracy numerical integration for other severities. The FFT approximation's moments (Est) are compared to the theoretical ones, and Err is the noise-aware relative error between them. The theoretical calculation is independent of the FFT, so close agreement is strong evidence the approximation is valid. When any unit can take negative values, SD replaces CV throughout. Rows failing a unit's validation_eps gate, or the portfolio's for the total, are emphasized. If any unit cedes, every block switches to the cession view: EX, Est and Err become Subject, Net (or Ceded) and Change, the effect of the cession, so the table no longer validates: validate the gross portfolio.
